/-- **The separated-presheaf property of the widened carrier**: base change of widened locally
certified divisor classes along a faithfully flat map of test algebras is injective.  Through
`classify`, base change is precomposition of the classifying morphism with `Spec` of the map,
which is an (effective) epimorphism. -/
theorem DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_injective_of_faithfullyFlat {S S' : Type u} [CommRing S]
    [Algebra k S] [CommRing S'] [Algebra k S'] [Algebra S S'] [IsScalarTower k S S']
    [Module.FaithfullyFlat S S'] :
    Function.Injective
      (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (C := C) (n := genus C) (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S S')) := by
  intro F G hFG
  haveI : EffectiveEpi (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S S'))) :=
    effectiveEpi_specMap_of_faithfullyFlat
  haveI : Epi ((Over.overSpecMap (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S S')).left) :=
    inferInstanceAs (Epi (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S S'))))
  haveI : Epi (Over.overSpecMap (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S S')) :=
    Over.epi_of_epi_left _
  have hc := congrArg (classify S') hFG
  rw [classify_mapAlgHom, classify_mapAlgHom] at hc
  exact (classify S).injective
    ((cancel_epi (Over.overSpecMap (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S S'))).mp hc)

/-- **Effective-epi descent of a widened divisor class along an étale cover**: a widened
locally certified divisor class over the carrier of an étale cover of `Spec A` whose two
coprojection pullbacks to the tensor square of the carrier agree descends, uniquely, to a class
over `A`.

The classifying morphism of `F` coequalizes the kernel pair of the covering morphism
`Spec E.Carrier ⟶ Spec A` (the kernel pair is `Spec` of the tensor square, by
`pullbackSpecIso`), so it factors through the effective epi; the factorization lands back in
the slice over `Spec k` by epi cancellation, and uniqueness is the separated-presheaf
property. -/
theorem DivFamZarAff.exists_descent_of_tensor_eq {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (F : DivFamZarAff C E.Carrier (genus C))
    (h : DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom
          ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft :
            E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) F
        = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom
          ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
            E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) F) :
    ∃! F₀ : DivFamZarAff C A (genus C),
      DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) F₀ = F := by
  classical
  haveI : EffectiveEpi (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier))) :=
    effectiveEpi_specMap_of_faithfullyFlat
  -- the double-pullback agreement of classifying morphisms, in the slice over `Spec k`
  have hOv : Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft :
          E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)
        ≫ classify E.Carrier F
      = Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
          E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)
        ≫ classify E.Carrier F := by
    rw [← classify_mapAlgHom, ← classify_mapAlgHom, h]
  -- hence the classifying morphism coequalizes the kernel pair of the covering morphism
  have hfstsnd : pullback.fst (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)))
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)))
        ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left
      = pullback.snd (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)))
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)))
        ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left := by
    rw [← cancel_epi (pullbackSpecIso A E.Carrier E.Carrier).inv,
      pullbackSpecIso_inv_fst_assoc, pullbackSpecIso_inv_snd_assoc]
    exact congrArg CommaMorphism.left hOv
  have hcoeq : ∀ {Z : Scheme.{u}} (g₁ g₂ : Z ⟶ Spec (.of E.Carrier)),
      g₁ ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier))
        = g₂ ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier))
      → g₁ ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left = g₂ ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left := by
    intro Z g₁ g₂ hg
    calc g₁ ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left
        = pullback.lift g₁ g₂ hg ≫ pullback.fst _ _ ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left := by

198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
327	
328	## Final report (your last message)
329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
339	not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.
340	
341	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
342	
343	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
344	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
345	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
346	`subagents` skill):
347	
348	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
349	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
350	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
351	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
352	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
353	
354	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

11	# Finite gluing of the rank-one evaluation divisor on a presentation carrier
12	
13	Over the Noetherian affine carrier of a tied rank-one presentation, the local evaluation
14	divisors produced on a finite spanning family of principal opens are compatible on pairwise
15	overlaps.  They therefore glue to an actual `DivFamZarAff` on the carrier.  Zariski separation
16	of `PicEtAff` identifies the Abel value of the glue with the represented input class, and
17	injectivity of the etale-plus unit identifies its relative Picard class with the presentation
18	representative.  The chosen local sections retain their exact Cech-class and native evaluation
19	identities.
20	
21	This is deliberately only a Noetherian, presentation-carrier result.  It does **not** descend
22	the glued divisor through the etale cover to the original algebra `A`, does not prove
23	independence of the chosen presentation, does not construct an arbitrary-scheme pullback
24	square, and does not produce `PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented`.
25	-/

12	/-!
13	# Faithfully-flat descent for the widened divisor functor, via representability
14	
15	The widened divisor functor `divFunctorAff C (genus C)` is representable
16	(`divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy`, `Picard/DivRepAffChallenge.lean`), and over an affine
17	test the functor value collapses to `DivFamZarAff` (`divFamZarAffAffineEquiv`,
18	`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffVehicle.lean`).  Composing the two turns a widened class over a test
19	algebra into a **classifying morphism** to the representing scheme, naturally in the algebra
20	(`divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_naturality`, `Picard/DivisorFamilyAffMap.lean`).
21	
22	This file cashes that in for descent: `Spec` of a faithfully flat ring map is quasi-compact,
23	surjective and flat, hence an **effective epimorphism** of schemes by the fpqc-subcanonicity
24	instance (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Fpqc.lean`).  Precomposition with an (effective) epi
25	is injective, so the widened divisor presheaf is *separated* along faithfully flat maps; and a
26	class over the carrier of an étale cover whose two coprojection pullbacks to the tensor square
27	agree has classifying morphism coequalizing the kernel pair of the cover (through
28	`pullbackSpecIso`), so it *descends*, uniquely, to the base ring.
29	
30	## Main declarations
31	
32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZarAff.classify` — the classifying equivalence
33	  `DivFamZarAff C S (genus C) ≃ (overSpec k S ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C)`, with naturality
34	  `DivFamZarAff.classify_mapAlgHom`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.effectiveEpi_specMap_of_faithfullyFlat` — `Spec` of a faithfully flat
36	  algebra map is an effective epimorphism.
37	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_injective_of_faithfullyFlat` — the
38	  separated-presheaf property of the widened carrier along faithfully flat maps.
39	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZarAff.exists_descent_of_tensor_eq` — effective-epi descent of a
40	  widened divisor class along an étale cover of the test algebra.
41	-/

82	            (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom φ F)) := rfl

84	          ((divFunctorAff C (genus C)).map (Over.overSpecMap φ).op
85	            ((divFamZarAffAffineEquiv C (genus C) S).symm F)) := by
86	        rw [← hnat, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]
87	        rfl
88	    _ = Over.overSpecMap φ ≫ (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv.symm
89	          ((divFamZarAffAffineEquiv C (genus C) S).symm F) :=
90	        ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).comp_homEquiv_symm _ _).symm
91	    _ = Over.overSpecMap φ ≫ classify S F := rfl
92	
93	/-- **`Spec` of a faithfully flat algebra map is an effective epimorphism** of schemes: it is
94	flat and surjective by `flat_and_surjective_SpecMap_iff`, quasi-compact because it is affine,
95	and quasi-compact surjective flat morphisms are effective epis by fpqc subcanonicity. -/
96	theorem effectiveEpi_specMap_of_faithfullyFlat {S S' : Type u} [CommRing S] [CommRing S']
97	    [Algebra S S'] [Module.FaithfullyFlat S S'] :
98	    EffectiveEpi (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S S'))) := by
99	  have hff : (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S S')).hom.FaithfullyFlat :=
100	    RingHom.faithfullyFlat_algebraMap_iff.mpr inferInstance
101	  obtain ⟨hflat, hsurj⟩ :=
102	    (flat_and_surjective_SpecMap_iff (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S S'))).mpr hff
103	  haveI := hflat
104	  haveI := hsurj
105	  infer_instance
106	
107	/-- **The separated-presheaf property of the widened carrier**: base change of widened locally
108	certified divisor classes along a faithfully flat map of test algebras is injective.  Through
109	`classify`, base change is precomposition of the classifying morphism with `Spec` of the map,
110	which is an (effective) epimorphism. -/
111	theorem DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_injective_of_faithfullyFlat {S S' : Type u} [CommRing S]
112	    [Algebra k S] [CommRing S'] [Algebra k S'] [Algebra S S'] [IsScalarTower k S S']
113	    [Module.FaithfullyFlat S S'] :
114	    Function.Injective
115	      (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (C := C) (n := genus C) (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S S')) := by
116	  intro F G hFG
117	  haveI : EffectiveEpi (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S S'))) :=
118	    effectiveEpi_specMap_of_faithfullyFlat
119	  haveI : Epi ((Over.overSpecMap (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S S')).left) :=
120	    inferInstanceAs (Epi (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S S'))))
121	  haveI : Epi (Over.overSpecMap (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S S')) :=
122	    Over.epi_of_epi_left _
123	  have hc := congrArg (classify S') hFG
124	  rw [classify_mapAlgHom, classify_mapAlgHom] at hc
125	  exact (classify S).injective
126	    ((cancel_epi (Over.overSpecMap (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S S'))).mp hc)
127	
128	/-- **Effective-epi descent of a widened divisor class along an étale cover**: a widened
129	locally certified divisor class over the carrier of an étale cover of `Spec A` whose two
130	coprojection pullbacks to the tensor square of the carrier agree descends, uniquely, to a class
131	over `A`.
132	
133	The classifying morphism of `F` coequalizes the kernel pair of the covering morphism
134	`Spec E.Carrier ⟶ Spec A` (the kernel pair is `Spec` of the tensor square, by
135	`pullbackSpecIso`), so it factors through the effective epi; the factorization lands back in
136	the slice over `Spec k` by epi cancellation, and uniqueness is the separated-presheaf
137	property. -/
138	theorem DivFamZarAff.exists_descent_of_tensor_eq {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
139	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (F : DivFamZarAff C E.Carrier (genus C))
140	    (h : DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom
141	          ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft :
142	            E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) F
143	        = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom
144	          ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
145	            E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) F) :
146	    ∃! F₀ : DivFamZarAff C A (genus C),
147	      DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) F₀ = F := by
148	  classical
149	  haveI : EffectiveEpi (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier))) :=
150	    effectiveEpi_specMap_of_faithfullyFlat
151	  -- the double-pullback agreement of classifying morphisms, in the slice over `Spec k`
152	  have hOv : Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft :
153	          E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)
154	        ≫ classify E.Carrier F
155	      = Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
156	          E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)
157	        ≫ classify E.Carrier F := by
158	    rw [← classify_mapAlgHom, ← classify_mapAlgHom, h]
159	  -- hence the classifying morphism coequalizes the kernel pair of the covering morphism
160	  have hfstsnd : pullback.fst (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)))
161	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)))
162	        ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left
163	      = pullback.snd (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)))
164	          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)))
165	        ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left := by
166	    rw [← cancel_epi (pullbackSpecIso A E.Carrier E.Carrier).inv,
167	      pullbackSpecIso_inv_fst_assoc, pullbackSpecIso_inv_snd_assoc]
168	    exact congrArg CommaMorphism.left hOv
169	  have hcoeq : ∀ {Z : Scheme.{u}} (g₁ g₂ : Z ⟶ Spec (.of E.Carrier)),
170	      g₁ ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier))
171	        = g₂ ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier))
172	      → g₁ ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left = g₂ ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left := by
173	    intro Z g₁ g₂ hg
174	    calc g₁ ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left
175	        = pullback.lift g₁ g₂ hg ≫ pullback.fst _ _ ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left := by
176	          rw [← Category.assoc, pullback.lift_fst]
177	      _ = pullback.lift g₁ g₂ hg ≫ pullback.snd _ _ ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left := by
178	          rw [hfstsnd]
179	      _ = g₂ ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left := by
180	          rw [← Category.assoc, pullback.lift_snd]
181	  -- descend the classifying morphism at the scheme level
182	  set w : Spec (.of A) ⟶ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left :=
183	    EffectiveEpi.desc (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)))
184	      (classify E.Carrier F).left hcoeq with hw
185	  have hfac : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)) ≫ w
186	      = (classify E.Carrier F).left := by
187	    rw [hw]; exact EffectiveEpi.fac _ _ _
188	  -- the over-triangle of the descended morphism, by epi cancellation
189	  have htri : w ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom = (overSpec k A).hom := by
190	    rw [← cancel_epi (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier))),
191	      ← Category.assoc, hfac, Over.w]
192	    show Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k E.Carrier))
193	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier))
194	          ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))
195	    rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k A E.Carrier, CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, Spec.map_comp]
196	  -- the descended class, through the slice-level factorization
197	  have hex : DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)
198	      ((classify A).symm (Over.homMk w htri)) = F := by
199	    apply (classify E.Carrier).injective
200	    rw [classify_mapAlgHom, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
201	    exact Over.OverMorphism.ext hfac
202	  refine ⟨(classify A).symm (Over.homMk w htri), hex, fun F₀ hF₀ => ?_⟩
203	  have hcan : IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A E.Carrier
204	      = (Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k := AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl
205	  apply DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_injective_of_faithfullyFlat (S := A) (S' := E.Carrier)
206	  rw [hcan, hF₀, hex]
207	
208	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	# Etale separatedness of the affine Picard plus construction
10	
11	Restriction of `PicEtAff` to the carrier of an etale cover is injective.  An equality
12	after restriction supplies a common refinement over the covering algebra.  Its carrier
13	is etale and faithfully flat over the original algebra by transitivity, so it can be
14	presented as a cover of the original algebra and used as a common refinement there.
15	-/

30	construction. -/

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import Mathlib.RingTheory.Etale.Field
7	import Mathlib.RingTheory.Smooth.Flat
8	import Mathlib.RingTheory.Flat.FaithfullyFlat.Algebra
9	import Mathlib.RingTheory.FinitePresentation
10	
11	/-!
12	# Presented étale covers of an affine base
13	
14	A (singleton, affine) *étale cover* of `Spec A` is a faithfully flat étale `A`-algebra `B`.
15	For the étale-sheafification (plus) construction of the relative Picard functor, the covers
16	of a fixed base must form a *small* directed index: this file realizes them as **presented**
17	covers — a number of variables `n` together with an ideal of `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A` whose
18	quotient is étale over `A` with `Spec` mapping onto `Spec A`.  The type of presented covers
19	of `A` lives in the same universe as `A`, while still capturing every étale cover up to
20	isomorphism of the carrier (`Algebra.EtaleCover.of` and its accessor `ofEquiv`).
21	
22	Surjectivity of the spectrum map is recorded instead of faithful flatness because it is
23	statable without flatness hypotheses; combined with flatness of étale algebras it *is*
24	faithful flatness (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_comap_surjective`), and that instance is
25	provided on the carrier.
26	
27	## Main declarations
28	
29	* `Algebra.EtaleCover A`: presented étale covers of `Spec A`, a `Type u` for `A : Type u`;
30	  `E.Carrier` is the covering algebra, with `Algebra.Etale A E.Carrier` and
31	  `Module.FaithfullyFlat A E.Carrier` instances.
32	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.of B hB`: any étale `A`-algebra `B` (with surjective spectrum map)
33	  underlies a presented cover, with carrier identification `Algebra.EtaleCover.ofEquiv`.
34	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.Refines`: `E'` refines `E` when the covering spectrum of `E'` maps
35	  to that of `E` over the base — a mere existence (`Prop`); the plus construction proves
36	  independence of the chosen refinement map, so no choice of map is carried here.
37	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.prod`: the common refinement `Spec (B ⊗[A] B')` of two covers, with
38	  refinement witnesses `prodInl`/`prodInr` — directedness of the index
39	  (`exists_refines_prod`).
40	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.self`: the trivial cover `Spec A` itself, refined by every cover
41	  (`refines_self`) — the base point of the index.
42	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChange`: the pulled-back cover along `A → A'`, with carrier
43	  `A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier` (`baseChangeEquiv`) and the canonical `A`-algebra map
44	  `baseChangeInclude` into it.
45	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`: over a field `K`, every cover
46	  is refined by a finite separable field extension of `K` (single-factor refinement) —
47	  field-extension covers are cofinal, the form the degree theory and Galois descent
48	  consume; `Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField` packages such an extension as a cover.
49	-/
50	
51	set_option autoImplicit false
52	
53	universe u
54	
55	open TensorProduct
56	
57	namespace Algebra
58	
59	/-- A presented étale cover of `Spec A`: a finite-variable polynomial presentation of an
60	étale `A`-algebra whose spectrum maps onto `Spec A`.  Presentations keep the type of covers
61	small (`Type u` for `A : Type u`), which is what makes the étale plus construction over
62	these covers a legitimate colimit; the carrier-level content is recovered by
63	`Algebra.EtaleCover.of`/`ofEquiv`. -/
64	structure EtaleCover (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : Type u where
65	  /-- The number of variables of the presentation. -/
66	  n : ℕ
67	  /-- The ideal of relations of the presentation. -/
68	  ideal : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)
69	  /-- The presented algebra is étale over the base. -/
70	  etale : Algebra.Etale A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ ideal)
71	  /-- The spectrum of the presented algebra covers the spectrum of the base. -/
72	  comap_surjective :
73	    Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ ideal)))
74	
75	namespace EtaleCover
76	
77	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
78	
79	/-- The covering algebra presented by an étale cover. -/
80	protected abbrev Carrier (E : EtaleCover A) : Type u :=
81	  MvPolynomial (Fin E.n) A ⧸ E.ideal
82	
83	instance (E : EtaleCover A) : Algebra.Etale A E.Carrier :=
84	  E.etale
85	
86	instance (E : EtaleCover A) : Module.FaithfullyFlat A E.Carrier :=
87	  .of_comap_surjective E.comap_surjective
88	
89	/-! ## Constructors -/
90	
91	section constructors
92	
93	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
94	
95	/-- Package an explicitly presented étale algebra with surjective spectrum map as a
96	presented étale cover: the ideal of relations is the kernel of the presenting
97	surjection. -/
98	noncomputable def ofSurjective
99	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B)))
100	    {n : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A →ₐ[A] B) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
101	    EtaleCover A where
102	  n := n
103	  ideal := RingHom.ker f
104	  etale := .of_equiv (Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf).symm
105	  comap_surjective := by
106	    haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A B := .of_comap_surjective hB
107	    haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ RingHom.ker f) :=
108	      .of_linearEquiv A B (Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf).toLinearEquiv
109	    exact PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
110	
111	/-- The carrier of `ofSurjective` is the presented algebra. -/
112	noncomputable def ofSurjectiveEquiv
113	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B)))
114	    {n : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A →ₐ[A] B) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
115	    (ofSurjective hB f hf).Carrier ≃ₐ[A] B :=
116	  Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf
117	
118	/-- Any étale `A`-algebra whose spectrum covers `Spec A` underlies a presented étale
119	cover.  The presentation is chosen (étale algebras are finitely presented, in particular
120	finitely generated); the choice is harmless because consumers only ever use the carrier
121	identification `ofEquiv`. -/
122	noncomputable def of (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
123	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B))) : EtaleCover A :=
124	  ofSurjective hB
125	    (Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial''.mp inferInstance).choose_spec.choose
126	    (Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial''.mp inferInstance).choose_spec.choose_spec
127	
128	/-- The carrier of `of B hB` is `B` itself. -/
129	noncomputable def ofEquiv (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
130	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B))) :
131	    (of B hB).Carrier ≃ₐ[A] B :=
132	  ofSurjectiveEquiv hB _ _
133	
134	end constructors
135	
136	/-! ## Refinement and directedness -/
137	
138	/-- `E'` refines `E`: the covering spectrum of `E'` maps to that of `E` over `Spec A`,
139	i.e. there is an `A`-algebra map from the carrier of `E` to that of `E'`.  This is a mere
140	existence: the plus construction proves that the induced maps on descent classes do not
